strategyDescription: TypeScript builds sublinear TF-IDF vectors over title (double weight) plus a URL-stripped 400-char body excerpt, picks the most central PR then up to 7 more by farthest-first (max-min cosine) as exemplar seeds. Models assign every other PR, in batches of 6, to the closest seed or to none; TypeScript groups by seed, drops seeds that attract nobody to unclassified, one describe call per cluster names it, and TypeScript validates coverage, uniqueness and ranking.
noveltyRationale: Divisive bisection is top-down with the model inventing partitions of the whole set; map-reduce chunked by PR number; pairwise used Jaccard edges; TF-IDF (40477786734-1) never ran. This one uses lexical statistics only to choose fixed exemplar anchors, then the model performs constrained nearest-exemplar classification of each PR against those anchors (k-medoids-like single pass). Cluster count and membership boundaries are bounded by the seeds, not invented by the model, and an explicit none option yields unclassified PRs.
validation: 44 PRs covered exactly once; all numbers known; ids unique; sizes match unique PR counts; ranking size desc then id asc; window matches corpus (checked independently with node)
